A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ToolEVO research. Text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D are readable and can be reliably matched despite pagination and layout changes.

before.justification: v3 reports original ToolQA-D experiments, API-variation analyses, component ablations, and case/error analyses in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical outcomes, including the main comparisons in Tables 2–4, ablations in Table 5, and error analysis in Table 7.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A retain the same MCTS procedure, cached rollouts, self-reflection, tool-update component, and supervised fine-tuning objective. Algorithm 1 is unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same seven ToolQA-D datasets, Easy/Hard tasks, and static, in-domain dynamic, and OOD dynamic API environments. Appendix B preserves the same API-variation scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the main comparisons, ablations, and appendix error analysis. The two newly cited related works are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Sections 5.1 and Appendices A.6–B retain the same splits, sample counts, model configurations, training settings, and three-shot greedy-decoding evaluation. Appendix C.3 preserves the same 50-error-sample analysis design.

E4.justification: The API-name, parameter, and response-format analyses in Figures 4–6, component ablations in Table 5, and self-reflection, tool-update, and error analyses in Appendix C are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both retain point-estimate accuracy and error-percentage reporting. Neither reports evaluation run/seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted trends, and qualitative outcomes are unchanged. For example, Table 4 retains ToolEVO's Easy/Hard averages of 61.6/28.3 for Llama3-8B and 65.3/27.7 for Qwen2-7B; Appendix C's error percentages and case outcomes also match.

T1.justification: The task and MDP definitions, Equations (1)–(6), and appendix mathematical descriptions are unchanged. No theorem, proof, assumption, or derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about adapting to tool variability through ToolEVO, introducing ToolQA-D, and achieving effective in-domain and OOD adaptation. The novelty claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning Static-SFT's reliance on outdated APIs and the benefits of reflection and tool updates are unchanged. Appendix C.3 retains the same discussion of remaining invocation errors and difficulties interpreting API responses.

D1.justification: Appendix A.6 preserves the hyperparameters, model versions, hardware, and software details; Appendix D preserves the prompts. The existing code link merely moves from the abstract to a footnote, while dataset-access information remains unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds citations to Yu et al. (2025), SimulPL, and Chen et al. (2025), C-3PO, within the existing tool-learning citation list, without expanding their discussion or changing the paper's positioning. AlphaMath's updated publication entry refers to the same previously cited work.

P1.justification: v5 adds an Acknowledgments section, converts the code-access statement to a footnote, and updates bibliographic metadata. The scientific prose and organization of the main sections and appendices otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The code-link relocation changes first-page spacing, and references and appendix example boxes undergo minor reflow. Existing scientific figures and tables retain their content, design, and captions; none is added or removed.

improvement.justification: v5 adds funding acknowledgments and limited citation/bibliographic updates, while relocating an already-present code link. Sections 3–5 and Appendices A–D preserve the same method, empirical evidence, interpretations, and reproducibility details. These editorial changes do not meaningfully strengthen or weaken the paper's overall quality.
